eips.title: LUCID encrypted mempool
eips.summary: The whole call reviewed Jannik's PR adding a validator-voted priority list of key publishers to LUCID, and the signing and ordering changes it brings.

moments.context: Jannik said he had opened a PR to the EIP about half an hour before the call, adding the key-publisher whitelisting mechanism.
Justin credited Jannik with opening the PR into Lucid, which specifies the top-of-block ordering mechanism the group converged on last session.
Jannik renamed the mechanism from whitelist to priority list, and split the PR into an EL voting contract and the CL ordering rules that consume it.
Key messages now carry a signature, so a transaction cannot claim its key came from a priority-listed publisher it did not use.
Max preceding commitments was removed, as Jannik found it difficult to combine with the priority-list ordering.
Justin committed to reviewing the PR, singled out the Engine API changes as needing attention, and said he would pull in Ander and Julian.
The top-of-block fee was kept: it is still needed to decide who gets into the size-constrained priority section under congestion.
Jannik flagged the key message signing format as unsatisfying, since it mixes RLP transaction signing with SSZ container signing and BLS is unavailable for EL addresses.

eips.title: Frame Transaction
eips.summary: Raised as a possible abstraction for the key message signing format, then set aside because a key message is not a transaction.

moments.context: Justin suggested frame transactions could abstract away the mixed RLP/SSZ signing format.
Jannik objected that a key message is not a transaction — it is a consensus-layer message that uses the execution-layer signing scheme.
Justin kept the door open: validating the origin of a key could be treated as a frame within a transaction, which would then need to read the key message.
